source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And there were at that time some reporting [or: telling] to the Galileans that Pilate had mingled [or: mixed] their blood with their sacrifices. And it happened that when he entered the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees to eat bread on the Sabbath, behold, they were watching him [closely].

translation_notes: מקצת (consonants קצת): Candidates: H7117 'a portion', H7118 same meaning. Chose H7117 because the מ- prefix + 'portion' = 'some of', fitting the narrative introduction of partial reporters.

ערב (consonants ערב): Candidates: H6148 'to intermix/braid', H6149 'to be agreeable', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Chose H6148 because 'mixed/mingled blood with sacrifices' produces a coherent image of Pilate mixing the blood of Galileans with their offerings.
עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5973 because 'mingled their blood WITH their sacrifices' is the only coherent reading.
בבית (consonants בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1006 'Bajith'. Chose H1004 because entering 'a house' of a Pharisee ruler is the natural image.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. Chose H259 because 'one of the rulers' is the natural reading.
משר (consonants שר): Candidates: H8269 'a head person/ruler', H8270 'a string/cord'. Chose H8269 because 'from a ruler of the Pharisees' fits the context of entering a prominent person's house.
פת (consonants פת): Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel of bread', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. Chose H6595 because 'to eat bread' is the coherent dining image.
textual_notes: The text appears to combine two separate narrative episodes: (1) a report about Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices, and (2) an entry into a Pharisee ruler's house on the Sabbath. The transition marker ונעשת ('and it happened') suggests a scene shift, but the consonantal text has no clear punctuation separating them.

ודמם could be parsed as 'and their blood' (דם + possessive suffix) or as the root דמם H1826 'to be silent/dumb'. Context of 'mixed with sacrifices' strongly favors 'their blood' as a noun with suffix.
והנם could be parsed as והנם 'and behold them' (demonstrative) rather than H2011 'Hinnom'. The watching context clearly supports 'and behold they'.

verses.literal: And they were in that time some telling to [the] Galileans and their blood mixed Pilate with their sacrifices and it happened when he entered in [the] house [of] one of [the] rulers [of] the Pharisees to eat bread on [the] Sabbath and behold they [were] watching him

verses.translation: And Yeshua answered [or: responded to] them: Do you think that those Galileans were sinners more than the other Galileans because they suffered these things? And behold, a certain man afflicted [with dropsy] was before him.

translation_notes: וענה (consonants ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because 'Yeshua answered them' fits the dialogue context.
להם: The ל prefix + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 as the 3mp pronoun 'to them', which is the natural reading in a dialogue.
הם (standalone): Candidates: H1990, H1991, H1992. Chose H1992 'they' as a copular emphasis: 'they [are] sinners'.
כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/that'. Chose H3588 because a causal conjunction fits: 'because they suffered these things'.
אלו (consonants אלו): Candidates: H431 'lo!/these', H432 'if'. Chose H431 as a demonstrative 'these', fitting 'things these'.
והנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' introduces a new observation in narrative.
איש (consonants איש): Candidates: H376 'a man', H377 'to act manly'. Chose H376 because 'a man one' = 'a certain man' fits the narrative.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. Chose H259 as 'one/a certain', modifying 'man'.
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to be/exist', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because 'was before him' is the coherent image.
textual_notes: משוקה is not in the provided candidates. The consonants suggest a passive participle from a root related to שקה (to water/irrigate) or possibly a medical condition term. In context — a man with an ailment standing before a healer — this likely refers to dropsy (excessive fluid), consistent with being 'watered/swollen'.
The text appears to merge two narrative threads: the discourse about the Galileans and the appearance of a sick man at the Pharisee's house. The transition at והנה marks the shift.

verses.literal: And answered Yeshua to them [Do you] think you that those Galileans they [are] sinners more than [the] Galileans the others because they suffered things these And behold a man one afflicted [with dropsy] was before him
[He is] saying not only if not you return all-of-you you will perish like
verses.amplified: [He is] saying, not only [this], [but] if you do not turn back [or: repent], all of you will perish [or: be destroyed] likewise
work: אומר (consonants א-ו-מ-ר): Candidate: H201 'Omar, grandson of Esau'. However, this is clearly a participial form from the root אמר (to say), functioning as 'saying/says'. The proper noun Omar makes no contextual sense in a sentence about warning and perishing. The Strong's lexicon provided only H201 for these consonants, but the form is transparently the Qal active participle of אמר (H559). Chose the verbal reading 'saying'.

רק (consonants ר-ק): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely', H7536 'spittle'. In the phrase 'not only if not you return', H7535 'only' produces the natural adverbial sense 'not merely/only'. H7534 'emaciated' or H7536 'spittle' produce nonsense here. Chose H7535.
אם (consonants א-מ): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Following 'not only', a conditional 'if' produces a coherent warning clause. 'Mother' makes no sense. Chose H518.
ambiguities: אומר: The Strong's candidates only list H201 (Omar, proper noun), but the consonants א-ו-מ-ר are clearly a participial form of אמר 'to say' (H559). The subject who is 'saying' is not stated in this section — presumably carried from prior context.
תשובו: No candidates provided. Root שוב (H7725) 'to turn back, return, repent' in 2mp imperfect. Could mean physical return or spiritual repentance; context of perishing suggests repentance.
תאבדו: No candidates provided. Root אבד (H6) 'to perish, be destroyed' in 2mp imperfect.
כולם: No candidates provided. כל + suffix ם = 'all of them/you'. In context functioning as 'all of you'.

verses.literal: them eighteen who upon-them fell the-tower in-Shiloah and-killed them do-you-think that-they were guilty more than all the-people the-ones-dwelling in-Jerusalem
verses.amplified: Those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam [or: Shiloah] fell and killed them — do you consider [or: reckon] that they were more guilty [or: indebted] than all the people dwelling in Jerusalem?
work: שמנה (consonants ש-מ-נ-ה): Candidates: H8083 'eight'; also sub-roots מנה H4487-4490 'weigh/portion/time'. Combined with the following עשר, 'eight-ten' = eighteen is the only coherent reading. Chose H8083.

עשר (consonants ע-ש-ר): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 'ten in combination (-teen)'. Following שמנה 'eight', this is the compound number form 'eight-teen' = eighteen. H6240 is the combining form. Chose H6240.

אשר (consonants א-ש-ר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. As a relative pronoun introducing 'upon whom the tower fell', H834 is the only coherent choice. Chose H834.

נפל (consonants נ-פ-ל): Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5308 'to fall (Aramaic)', H5309 'abortion/something fallen'. A tower falling upon people — H5307 'to fall' is the clear verbal reading. Chose H5307.

המגדל (consonants ה-מ-ג-ד-ל): The ה is the definite article. Candidates for מגדל: H4026 'a tower'. Sub-root גדל H1431-1435 offers 'great/magnitude/thread/Giddel', but with the מ prefix and in context of something that 'fell upon them', 'the tower' is the only coherent reading. Chose H4026.

והרג (consonants ו-ה-ר-ג): Candidates: H2026 'to smite with deadly intent', H2027 'slaughter'. The ו is conjunctive. As a verb completing the sequence 'fell...and killed them', H2026 is the verbal form. Chose H2026.

על (consonants ע-ל): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God/aloft', H5921 'above/over/upon/against', H5922 (Aramaic), H5923 'a yoke'. Here introducing comparison 'more than all the people', H5921 'over/above/than' fits. Chose H5921.
ambiguities: בשיבסי: No candidates provided. This appears to be a Hebrew transliteration of a place name. The consonants ב-ש-י-ב-ס-י suggest 'in Shiloah/Siloam' (בשלחי would be more standard for Siloam/Shiloah). The ס instead of ל and the specific spelling suggest this may be a variant or corrupted transliteration of the place name known as Siloam.
תחשבו: No candidates provided. Root חשב (H2803) 'to think, reckon, consider' in 2mp imperfect.
חייבים: No candidates provided. From a root חיב meaning 'guilty, liable, indebted' — a term common in later/Mishnaic Hebrew. The ים suffix here is a standard masculine plural: 'guilty ones'.
יות%ר: No candidates provided. From יתר (H3498) 'to remain, be left over'; the form יותר functions as an adverb meaning 'more/exceedingly' in later Hebrew.

verses.literal: I saying to-you that-if not you-return you-will-be lost-ones like-them
verses.amplified: I say [or: am telling] you that if you do not turn back [or: repent], you will be lost [or: perished, destroyed] just like them
work: אני (consonants א-נ-י): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. As subject of 'saying to you', H589 'I' is the only coherent reading. Chose H589.
שאם (ש + א-מ): The ש functions as the relative/conjunction 'that'. Candidates for אם: H517 'mother', H518 'if/conditional'. 'That if you do not return' is coherent; 'that mother' is not. Chose H518.
ambiguities: אומ%ר: No candidates provided for this form. Clearly from root אמר (H559) 'to say', here as a participle 'saying' or understood as present tense 'say'.
תשובו: No candidates provided. Root שוב (H7725) 'to turn back, return, repent' in 2mp imperfect. Same form as section 1.
תהיו: No candidates provided. Root היה (H1961) 'to be/become' in 2mp imperfect: 'you will be'.

אבודים: No candidates provided. From root אבד (H6) 'to perish/be lost', a passive/stative participle with masculine plural suffix: 'lost ones / perished ones'. The ים here is a standard plural marker as the verb תהיו is also 2mp.

כא%לו: No candidates provided. כ (like/as) + אלו (these/those/them). Could also be parsed as כ + אל + ו, but 'like those/like them' is the most natural reading in context, paralleling כמו in section 1.

verses.translation: And he said to them this parable: A certain man had a fig tree in his vineyard, and he came to look for [its] fruit but did not find [any].

translation_notes: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — standard narrative 'and he said'.
להם: H3859 'to rankle' makes no sense. הם candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — ל + הם = 'to them'.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — demonstrative 'this' introducing the parable.

המשל: Candidates: H4910 'to rule', H4911 'to use figurative language', H4912 'a parable/maxim/allegory', H4913 'Mashal (place)', H4914 'a satire', H4915 'empire/parallel', H7944 'a fault', H7945 'on account of'. Chose H4912 — 'the parable', with ה prefix, as the noun being pointed to by 'this'.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 — 'a man/person', the subject of the parable.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one' = 'a certain [man]'.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 — 'there was to him' = 'he had'.
ולא (לא): H3808 'not' vs H3809 same (Aramaic). Chose H3808 — 'and not' + found = 'did not find'.
מצא: H4672 'to find/attain'. Only candidate. 'He found [none]'.
textual_notes: ע%ץ and תא%נה — The % marks appear to be scribal/manuscript artifacts. Reading as עץ ('tree') and תאנה ('fig tree'). Neither has Strong's candidates provided but these are standard Hebrew words (H6086 and H8384 respectively).
לבק%ש — reading as לבקש, infinitive of בקש 'to seek/search for', with % as manuscript artifact.

verses.literal: And he said to them this [is] the parable a man one there was to him [a] tree [of] fig in his vineyard and he came to seek the fruit and not he found

verses.translation: And he said to the keeper [or: guardian] of the vineyard: Already three years have passed that I have been asking for fruit from this fig tree, and I find none. Therefore uproot it, for it is consuming [or: devouring] the goodness [or: richness, praise-worthy yield] of the soil.

translation_notes: ואמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard narrative continuation.
הכרם (כרם): Candidates: H3754 'a vineyard/garden', H3755 'a vinedresser', H7410 'Ram'. Chose H3754 — 'the vineyard', the setting of the parable.
כבר: Candidates: H3527 'to augment/accumulate', H3528 'long ago/already/hitherto', H3529 'Kebar (river)', H1247–H1252 (בר variants). Chose H3528 — 'already', indicating the time that has elapsed.
שלש: Candidates: H8027 'to be triplicate/three', H8028 'Shelesh', H8029 'great grandchild'. Chose H8027 — the numeral 'three' modifying שנים.

שנים: H8147 'two/twofold'. However, in context שנים here must mean 'years' (from שנה, H8141). The consonants שנים can represent the plural of שנה. The candidate H8147 is for the numeral 'two' but the same consonants spell 'years'. Context with שלש ('three') demands 'years'.
שאני (אני): H589 'I' vs H590 'ship'. Chose H589 — ש + אני = 'that I [am]'.
זו: Candidates: H2097 'this/that', H2098 'this/that', H2099 'Ziv (month)'. Chose H2097 — demonstrative 'this' referring to the fig tree.
לזה (זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — ל + זה = 'for this [reason]' / 'therefore'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 — causal conjunction 'for/because'.

שבח: Candidates: H7623 'to address loudly/praise/pacify', H7624 'to adore'. Chose H7623 — here used as a noun meaning 'praise/goodness/excellence'. The fig tree is consuming the richness/goodness of the soil. In later Hebrew שבח carries the sense of 'praise/excellence/the best of'.
האדמה: Candidates: H126 'Admah (place)', H127 'soil/ground', H128 'Adamah (place)'. Chose H127 — 'the ground/soil', what the fruitless tree is depleting.
textual_notes: שנים — The consonants can be H8147 'two' or the plural of שנה 'year'. Since it follows שלש ('three'), it must mean 'years' (three years), not 'two'.
שבח האדמה — 'the goodness/richness of the ground'. שבח could mean 'praise' or 'the best quality'. The image is of the tree consuming the soil's nutrients/goodness without producing fruit.
The apostrophe mark (') after מוצ%א appears to be a scribal notation or paragraph marker, not a translatable element.
לשומ%ר — reading as לשומר, 'to the keeper/guardian'. The % is a manuscript artifact.

verses.literal: And he said to the keeper of the vineyard already passed three years that I [am] asking fruit from fig [tree] this and I am not finding therefore uproot it for it [is] consuming [the] goodness of the ground

verses.translation: And he answered him: Lord [or: Master], leave the fig tree [for] this year, and I will dig around it and surround it [with] manure [or: fertilizer].

translation_notes: והוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/she/it', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 — 'and he' as the subject pronoun introducing the keeper's reply.

ענה: Candidates: H6030 'to heed/respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 'to answer (Aramaic)', H6033 'to afflict (Aramaic)', H6034 'Anah'. Chose H6030 — 'answered', the natural response verb in dialogue.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller/lord', H114 'Addon (person)'. Chose H113 — 'lord/master', the keeper addressing the vineyard owner.

הנח: The candidate H5146 'Noah' is irrelevant. This is the hiphil imperative of נוח 'to rest/leave/permit' — 'leave [it]' or 'let [it] be'. No appropriate Strong's number from the candidates provided.

שנה: Candidates: H8138 'to fold/duplicate/transmute', H8139 'sleep (Aramaic)', H8140 'a year (Aramaic)', H8141 'a year', H8142 'sleep', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H8141 — 'year', modified by זו 'this' = 'this year'.
זו: Candidates: H2097 'this/that', H2098 'this/that', H2099 'Ziv'. Chose H2097 — demonstrative 'this' modifying 'year'.
textual_notes: הנח — The only Strong's candidate is H5146 'Noah', which is clearly wrong. This is the hiphil imperative of נוח (H3240, 'to cause to rest/leave/permit'). The Strong's list provided is incomplete for this word.
זבלים — no Strong's candidates provided. This is post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew for 'manure/dung/fertilizer' (related to H2083 זבל).

verses.literal: And he answered him lord leave the fig tree year this and I will dig around it and I will surround it [with] manure

verses.translation: And if it produces fruit, [that is] well [or: good]; but if not, I will cut it down [or: destroy it].

translation_notes: ואם (both): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — conditional conjunction 'and if', introducing both the positive and negative outcomes.
פרי: H6529 'fruit'. Only candidate.
מוטב: H2869 'good' (Aramaic). The form מוטב is a later Hebrew expression meaning 'it is good/well' — a positive outcome.
לאו: H176 'or/if'. With ל prefix this forms לאו, a later Hebrew negation meaning 'no/not' — 'and if not'.
textual_notes: אכריתנה — parsed as אכרית + נה (1cs imperfect hiphil of כרת 'to cut off' + 3fs suffix 'it'). This means 'I will cut it off/down' — referring to the fig tree. The speaker here appears to be the vineyard keeper, who conditionally agrees to destroy the tree if it still bears no fruit.

verses.literal: And if it makes fruit [that is] good and if not I will cut it off

verses.translation: And on the following [or: next] Sabbath, he was in their synagogue [or: house of assembly], on [one of the] Sabbaths.

translation_notes: הבאה: H872 'an entrance to a building' is the only candidate, but this reading produces an awkward image ('the entrance'). The consonants באה can also represent the feminine qal participle of בוא 'to come' = 'the coming [one]', i.e. 'the next/following'. In context, 'the coming Sabbath' = 'the next Sabbath' is far more coherent than 'the entrance'. Chose to read as participle of בוא (H935) though only H872 was listed.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 — 'he was/existed', a past-tense copula describing his location.
שלהם: להם candidates: H3859 'to rankle'. הם candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — ש + ל + הם = 'that of them' / 'their', a possessive construction.
textual_notes: וב5בת and ב5בתות — The numeral 5 embedded in these words appears to be a scribal artifact or encoding issue. Reading as ובשבת ('and on the Sabbath') and בשבתות ('on Sabbaths') respectively. שבת = H7676 'Sabbath'.
בב%ית — reading as בבית 'in the house of'. The % is a manuscript artifact. בית = H1004.
הכנסת — 'the assembly/synagogue'. This is a post-biblical Hebrew term (בית הכנסת = 'house of gathering/synagogue'). No Strong's number in classical Hebrew.

The final phrase בשבתות ('on Sabbaths') seems somewhat redundant after 'on the coming Sabbath'. It may serve to specify that this was his custom on Sabbaths, or it may indicate 'on one of the Sabbaths' as a temporal marker.

verses.literal: And on [the] Sabbath the coming he was in [the] house of the assembly their on Sabbaths

verses.translation: And look — a certain woman who had been afflicted [or: ill] for eighteen years from a disease that completely [or: wholly] bent her — the Jebusite [affliction] — and she was walking as one bowing down, without [the] ability to look upward

translation_notes: שמנה (consonants שמנה): Candidates: H8083 'eight', H4487 'to weigh out', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H8083 because it pairs with עשר to form 'eighteen', matching the duration of illness described.

שנים (consonants שנים): H8147 'two/twofold' — but here contextually this is שנים meaning 'years' (from שנה H8141), the plural form; the candidate list only shows H8147 but the word clearly functions as 'years' in context of a time duration following 'eighteen'.

כלם (consonants כלם): H3637 'to wound/taunt/insult/humiliate'. Could read as כֻּלָּם 'all of them' (from כל H3605 with suffix). In context 'all of them the eighteen' seems to emphasize the totality of the eighteen years of illness. Reading as 'all of them' fits better than 'humiliate'.

למעלה (consonants למעלה): Candidates: H4608 'elevation/upward', H5927 'to ascend', H5929 'leaf'. Chose H4608 because 'to look upward' is a coherent physical image of someone bent over who cannot straighten up.
textual_notes: The word כלם could be read as כֻּלָּם 'all of them' (referring to the eighteen years) or from H3637 meaning 'humiliation/wounding'. The context of illness duration favors 'all of them' but a reading of 'humiliation' (a disease of humiliation for eighteen years) is also plausible.

היבוסי 'the Jebusite' is puzzling in a medical context. It may be a textual corruption or a colloquial/coded term for a particular type of affliction. The Jebusite identification (H2983) is the only consonantal match provided.
The % markers and numerical notation הי״ח suggest scribal annotations or damaged text. הי״ח appears to be an abbreviation for 'the eighteen' using Hebrew numerals יח.

verses.literal: And behold a woman one [who] had been ill eighteen years from illness of all the eighteen the Jebusite and walking as bowing without ability to look upward

verses.translation: And Yeshua saw her and called [to] her and said to her: Woman, your illness has departed [or: turned away, been removed]

translation_notes: ישוע (consonants ישוע): H3442 and H3443 both refer to Jeshua/Yeshua. Chose H3442 as the primary entry for the proper name.
ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates include H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a speech verb introducing direct discourse.

סרה (consonants סרה): H5626 'Sirah, a cistern' vs H5627 'apostasy/remission/turning aside'. Chose H5627 because the sense of 'departure/remission' fits perfectly: 'your illness has departed.' The root סור means to turn aside/depart, and סרה as a noun means removal or turning away.
textual_notes: The < symbol in א<ה suggests a damaged or uncertain letter. The word likely reads אשה (woman/wife) based on context — Yeshua addressing the ill woman.

verses.literal: And saw her Yeshua and called her and said to her woman departed [is] your illness

verses.translation: And he laid [his] hands upon her, and immediately she stood [upright] in her [full] stature and praised God [the Mighty One]

translation_notes: עליה (consonants עליה): H5944 'upper room/lofty place'. However, in context this is clearly עָלֶיהָ 'upon her' (preposition על + 3fs suffix). The candidate H5944 shares consonants but the prepositional reading is the obvious contextual fit.
ומיד (consonants ומיד): Contains יד H3027 'hand'. However, ומיד here functions as the adverb 'immediately' (literally 'from hand' = 'at once'), a well-known Hebrew idiom.
עמדה (consonants עמדה): H5979 'a station/domicile'. However, this is clearly the verb עמד 'to stand' in 3fs perfect form. She stood up in her full height.

האל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/Mighty One', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because with the definite article ה, האל means 'the God/the Mighty One' — she praised God after being healed.

verses.literal: And he placed the hands upon her and immediately she stood in her stature and praised God

verses.translation: And [those] in the house of the assembly [synagogue], full of fury [or: rage], answered and said: Six days they [are] in the week in which a person is able to do his work — and in those days the healer [physician] is able to occupy himself with the healing of the sick, and not on the Sabbath

translation_notes: וענו (consonants ענו): H6035 'humble/depressed'. However, this is clearly the verb ענה 'to answer' in 3mp perfect with vav consecutive. The consonantal form ענו matches both, but in narrative context 'and they answered' is the correct reading.
בבית (consonants בית): H1004 'house' vs H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because בבית הכנסת is 'in the house of the assembly' — a synagogue.
ששת (consonants שת): H8351 'tumult', H8352 'Seth', H8353 'six'. Chose H8353 because ששת ימים 'six days' is the clear contextual meaning preceding 'days'.
הם (consonants הם): H1992 'they' fits as the copula: 'six days they are in the week'.

האל: Candidates H408 'not', H410 'mighty/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. None of these fit well. However, the consonants here likely represent a defective or unusual spelling. textual_notes: האל: This is the most problematic word in the section. The Strong's candidates (not, mighty/God, these, to) do not produce a coherent image after 'shaking/gnashing of.' The expected word would be שנים (teeth). האל may be a scribal variant, a later Hebrew form, or a textual corruption. I have tentatively read it as 'the teeth' based on contextual demand (weeping + gnashing of teeth is a well-known Hebrew idiom for distress), but this reading requires a form not attested in the provided dictionary entries.
והרעשת: Likely from the root רעש (to shake/quake, H7493) in a causative or nominal form + construct ending ת. 'The shaking/quaking of' = gnashing/grinding, describing teeth.

verses.literal: And behold those who were first

verses.translation: In that very moment [certain ones] drew near to him, and some [or: a portion] of the Pharisees said to him, Go away from us, for Herod desires [or: is willing] to put you to death

translation_notes: שעה (שעה): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a moment'. Chose H8160 because 'in that moment' is the natural temporal phrase introducing a narrative event.
ומקצת (קצת): Candidates: H7117 'a portion', H7118 'a portion (Aramaic)'. Both mean the same; chose H7117 as the Hebrew form. 'And some of the Pharisees' fits the context of a subset approaching.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because'. Chose H3588 because this is clearly a causal conjunction introducing the reason for the warning.

אבה: Candidates: H14 'to breathe after/be acquiescent/desire', H15 'longing', H16 'papyrus'. Chose H14 because a verb meaning 'to desire/be willing' fits perfectly with the infinitive 'to kill you' that follows.

verses.literal: In that moment [they] approached him and some of the Pharisees said to him go from us for Herod desires to kill you

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to them, Go and tell that fox [or: jackal] that I am casting out [or: driving out] demons and performing healings — on the third day I will be complete [or: finished, perfected] and ceased [or: at an end]

translation_notes: ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua (name)', H3443 same. Chose H3442 as the standard entry for the personal name.

אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because a finite verb 'said' is required by the narrative syntax.
להם: The prefix ל + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — 'to them' is the natural indirect object here.

שועל: Candidates: H7776 'a jackal/fox', H7777 'Shual (name)'. Also על candidates but שועל as a whole word is clearly H7776 'fox/jackal' — Yeshua is calling Herod a fox, which fits the warning about Herod in the prior section.

מגרש: Candidates: H4054 'suburb/open country', H1643 'grain', H1644 'to drive out/expel', H1645 'produce'. Chose H1644 because 'driving out demons' is the coherent action described here — a participle form of גרש 'to drive out'.
תם: Candidates: H8535 'complete/pious/gentle', H8536 'there', H8537 'completeness/innocence'. Chose H8535 because 'I will be complete' paired with 'and ended' describes the conclusion of his work.
ואפס: Candidates: H656 'to disappear/cease', H657 'cessation/end'. Chose H656 as a verb form paralleling 'I will be complete' — 'and I will cease/come to an end'.
textual_notes: ה<דים and ה<לישי have damaged/missing consonants (marked with <). From context, ה<דים is almost certainly השדים (demons/shedim) and ה<לישי is השלישי (the third). These reconstructions are based on narrative logic but the actual consonants are incomplete.

תם ואפס could be read as two nouns ('completion and cessation') or as adjective + verb. The phrase 'I will be תם ואפס' likely means 'I will be finished and done' — describing the completion of his mission.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said to them go and say to that fox that I [am] driving out demons and doing healings on the third day I will be complete and ended

verses.translation: Only [or: nevertheless] it is required of me tomorrow and the day coming after it to walk [or: to journey], for it is not fitting that a prophet should be seen [or: should perish] outside of Jerusalem

translation_notes: רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/although', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'only/nevertheless' is the natural adverbial conjunction opening a qualifying statement.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because'. Chose H3588 — causal conjunction introducing the reason.
אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 because 'there is not fitting' = 'it is not fitting' is the natural construction.
שנביא: Candidates: H5029 'a prophet (Aramaic)', H5030 'a prophet/inspired man'. Chose H5030 as the Hebrew form. The ש prefix is the relative particle 'that'.

יראה: The consonants ירא + ה could be from ראה 'to see' (niphal: 'be seen') or from H3374 'fear/reverence'. In context, 'a prophet should perish' is the expected meaning (paralleling Luke 13:33 tradition), but the consonants יראה most naturally read as a niphal of ראה — 'should be seen/should appear'. However, this could also be a scribal form meaning 'should perish' from a different root. I've assigned H3374 as the listed candidate but the reading 'be seen/appear' from ראה is more likely.
textual_notes: למחףרת has a damaged consonant (marked with ף). This is almost certainly למחרת 'for the morrow/next day'.

יראה is genuinely ambiguous: the consonants could be niphal of ראה 'to be seen/appear' or could relate to H3374 'fear'. The expected meaning in this context of prophets and Jerusalem is 'should perish' (from אבד), but that root is not present. 'Should be seen/should appear outside of Jerusalem' makes reasonable sense — it is not fitting for a prophet to appear/meet his end outside Jerusalem. The Strong's candidate H3374 is the only one listed, but the consonants more naturally parse as a niphal form of ראה (H7200).

verses.literal: Only [it is] required of me for the morrow for the day coming after it to walk for there is not [it is] fitting that a prophet should be seen outside of Jerusalem

verses.translation: Jerusalem, [you] that kill the prophets and stone those sent [or: commissioned] to you — how many times I longed [or: desired] to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing [or: able]

translation_notes: כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', or כ + מה where H4100 'what/how'. Chose H4100 with prefix כ — 'how many' is the natural reading before 'times' (פעמים).
תחת: Candidates: H8478 'underneath/below', H8479 same (Aramaic), H8480 'Tachath (name)'. Chose H8478 because 'under her wings' is the coherent physical image of a hen sheltering chicks.
ולא: Chose H3808 'not' — simple negation 'and not'.
textual_notes: יכולתי — the consonants appear to be a first-person form ('I was able'), but contextually the meaning seems to be 'you (Jerusalem) were not willing' (second person). This may reflect a textual variant where the final word is ולא אביתם/יכלתם (you were not willing/able) condensed. The manuscript reads as first person 'I was not able' which is also a valid reading: 'and I was not able [to gather them]'.

verses.literal: [Jerusalem] that kills the prophets and stones the [ones] sent to you how many times I desired to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings and you were not willing

verses.translation: And behold, your house will be abandoned [or: left desolate], without [any] inhabitant. And I say that this will not be [or: this shall not happen]

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', or from נה H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' is the natural exclamatory introduction to a prophetic declaration.
מאין: From מ + אין. Candidates for אין: H369 'non-entity/negative', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'from without' = 'without' or 'devoid of', modifying 'one inhabiting'.
ואני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — 'and I' is the obvious reading as subject of 'say'.
שזה: ש + זה. Candidates for זה: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'that this' introduces the declaration.
לא: H3808 'not' — simple negation.
textual_notes: The phrase 'שזה לא יהיה' is ambiguous: it could mean 'that this will not happen' (i.e., you will not see me) or could be an incomplete sentence trailing into a following section. The text as it stands reads as a self-contained prophetic warning.

verses.literal: And behold your house will be left without [one] inhabiting and I say that this will not be
